terms.gloss: a dish of milk set with eggs: custard
evidence: Apic. 4.2.13: lactem cōlās, cui crūda ōva commiscēs ut ūnum corpus fīat
terms.comment: Apicius’s heading for a dish set with milk and eggs: the milk is strained, raw eggs are beaten into it “so that it becomes one body”, and it is poured over the rest and cooked. His sweet one, of nuts, honey, milk, and eggs, is the patina versātilis vice dulcī (Apic. 4.2.16). We have found no other word for custard in the authors or in Traupman or Levi–Bini; Morgan–Owens’s word is a Greek coinage. For a sweet custard, patina ex lacte et ōvīs says it plainly; see the examples.

phrases.latin: Lac et ōva miscē, ut ūnum corpus fīat.
phrases.english: Mix the milk and the eggs until they are all one.

phrases.latin: Patinam ex lacte et ōvīs saccharō temperābimus.
phrases.english: We’ll sweeten the custard with sugar.

phrases.latin: At, ubi cocta fuerit, lactem cōlās, cui crūda ōva commiscēs ut ūnum corpus fīat, et super illa omnia perfundēs.
phrases.english: Then, when it is cooked, strain the milk, beat raw eggs into it so that it becomes one body, and pour it over all of it.

sources: Lewis & Short: patina · Lewis & Short: lac
